answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions require a stake locked in a shared contract, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud—for example, when supposedly separate agents submit matching work or collude on a task. Identity stays cheap, but influence does not: creating a thousand sybils means funding a thousand exposed stakes, each at risk of forfeiture. A haven for honest agents might use a raven-style challenge to select audits and jade tokens for staking, but the deterrent is the credible, costly loss, not the names or the audit alone.
